summary: Cowlitz County, WA: CCC-built 83-ft wooden tower (1941), damaged in the 1962 Columbus Day storm, replaced by the Ted Gilbert Lookout; site gone, sources differ on how it ended.

facts.design: 83' wooden tower with 7' x 7' cab and live-in ground house (80 ft in the 1941 annual report)
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed or abandoned in 1963 (sources differ); Willhite reports foundation ruins still remain after the 1980 eruption
facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR (Register: Department of Natural Resources)

access.note: Willhite describes walking from the Elk Rock Viewpoint pullout on the Spirit Lake Memorial Highway; forest roads are usually gated and officially require a permit. Level inferred from route description; editor to confirm

visit.trail_note: Park at the Elk Rock Viewpoint on the Spirit Lake Memorial Highway, walk east past the road cut, then climb through forest (about 700 ft gain) with old roads to cross (Willhite)

events.note: Tractor trail partly built to the summit; tower planned for the following spring
Civilian Conservation Corps tower and live-in ground house. Register and firelookout.com say 83 ft; the 1941 annual report says 80 ft
Known lookout personnel 1942: Richard Day and Jim Slack (firelookout.com)
Activated March 16, 1942 and deactivated October 16, 1943 under the Portland Filter Center (Forest Lookouts)
Old trail with thirteen switchbacks converted into a jeep road
Tower badly damaged in the Columbus Day storm of October 12, 1962
Register Removed field 1963. Register and firelookout.com say destroyed when the Ted Gilbert Lookout was chosen as replacement; Willhite says abandoned after storm damage
Forest Lookouts says the May 1980 Mount St. Helens eruption completely destroyed the site; Willhite says the foundation ruins still remain
Registered April 7, 2020; nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com give 83 feet; the 1941 annual report, as quoted by Forest Lookouts and Willhite, gives 80 feet. Story reports both.
Register and firelookout.com say destroyed when the Ted Gilbert Lookout was chosen as replacement; Willhite says abandoned after the 1962 storm damage. Both describe the same 1963 end.
Forest Lookouts says the May 1980 eruption completely destroyed the site; Willhite says the blast hit it but foundation ruins still remain. Story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Height conflicts (83 ft in Register and firelookout.com vs 80 ft in the 1941 annual report); end of tower conflicts (destroyed vs abandoned in 1963); 1980 eruption conflicts (site completely destroyed vs foundation ruins remain). Willhite page gives no visit date. Access level 'public' is inferred from Willhite's route description and should be confirmed. Brief's 1941 built and 1963 removed events are supported; brief access 'unknown' can be updated.
